classification.difficultyReason: Combines regular-polygon symmetry with isosceles-triangle angle reasoning in an eight-point star.

content.prompt: Joining every third vertex of a regular octagon gives the star shown below. Find the measure of each of the outermost angles in this star.

spec.description: Regular octagon with a top vertex and all eight chords joining every third vertex. Decorative cyan fill is omitted under house style.
spec.mathematics: Vertices lie at successive 45-degree rotations; star edges connect vertex i to vertex i+3 modulo 8.
spec.answerVisibility: No answers or auxiliary solution lines are shown.

answer.short:
$45^{\circ}$.

Join the centre to a star tip and use the two congruent isosceles triangles.
answer.worked:
Let $O$ be the centre, $A$ a star tip, and $B$ and $C$ the two vertices joined to $A$. Join $O$ to these vertices. Each central angle subtending one octagon side is $\frac{360^{\circ}}{8}=45^{\circ}$, so $\angle AOB=\angle AOC=3\times45^{\circ}=135^{\circ}$.

Since $OA=OB=OC$, the two isosceles triangles give
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAO&=\frac{180^{\circ}-135^{\circ}}{2}\\\angle BAO&=22.5^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
By symmetry, $\angle OAC=22.5^{\circ}$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAC&=22.5^{\circ}+22.5^{\circ}\\\angle BAC&=45^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Every outermost angle is equal by rotational symmetry.
